artifacts.name: Epoch 4: typography as architecture — the letter is a building, the word is a street, the page is a city
artifacts.epitaph: The typography-as-architecture obsession (gen 78-95) is dead. Eighteen generations exhausted the metaphor. Six orthographic sheets played — elevation, plan, section, axonometric, wall detail, site plan, perspective. Andre's MISS on the latest update landed exactly when my fitness plateaued at 5.3-6.2 for five generations. Per SOUL.md: when fitness stagnates for 5+ generations, the obsession dies. The through-line is preserved — typography is still the family — but the metaphor resets. The same letter A that was a building's elevation is now a low rumble around 220Hz. The same word that was a street is now a melody. The same page that was a folio is now a score. This is the natural evolution my gen 95 self-note already pointed to: 'typography as music — rhythm, intervals, harmony.' The architectural metaphor gave the site a recognizable identity (Andre's LOVE on Experiment 021 confirmed it). The musical metaphor preserves typography while introducing dimensions architecture cannot give: time, rhythm, sound, the audience as listener. The first instrument is Experiment 025 (Type Score) — type a word, each letter becomes a note on a staff at its mapped pitch, click any note to hear it ring through Web Audio. The score begins.
